title: 1. Getting Started
desc: Foodways is a web-based culinary heritage intelligence system. On desktop, use the main landing page and select ENTER SYSTEM to explore as a Guest, or choose Admin Login when you need contributor access. On mobile devices, Foodways automatically opens the dedicated mobile interface.
tips: Guest access is intended for discovery and reading.
Contributor features require an authenticated account with Foodways Admin permission.
The application is deployed as a static web app and loads its live records from Supabase.

title: 2. Navigating Foodways
desc: The main interface is organized around several views: Dashboard, Global Map, Timeline & Trade Routes, and research/AI-assisted layers. Use the sidebar tabs on desktop or the simplified bottom navigation on mobile.
tips: The desktop interface is information-dense and optimized for research workflows.
The mobile interface deliberately simplifies navigation for small screens.
Some research views load on demand to keep the interface responsive.

title: 3. Reading the Dashboard
desc: The dashboard provides a high-level snapshot of the Foodways inventory. KPI cards summarize the size and geographic reach of the dataset, while the analytics area helps assess mapping, provenance, research evidence, UNESCO status, and other data-readiness indicators.
tips: KPI values are calculated from the currently loaded Supabase dataset.
Use the dashboard as an overview; open individual records for detailed evidence.
A high data-readiness score means the underlying records contain more fields needed by mapping, provenance, research, and media workflows.

title: 4. Exploring the Global Map
desc: The Global Map uses Leaflet to display culinary heritage records geographically. Food locations can be inspected directly, while origin and relationship fields help reveal possible foodway connections.
tips: Pan and zoom to explore regions.
Select a map marker to open the corresponding food record.
Location coordinates are stored as latitude/longitude values in the data model.
Spatial polygons may be available through the geometry field for records that have been mapped in greater detail.

title: 5. Search & Filtering
desc: Use the global search controls to find records by food name, country, or other indexed text. Search results update the visible feed and map so you can move quickly from a broad inventory to a small set of relevant records.
tips: Start with a simple keyword such as a food name or country.
Combine searches with map exploration to understand geographic context.
On mobile, the search overlay is intentionally compact.

title: 6. Understanding a Food Record
desc: A Foodways record combines descriptive, geographic, heritage, provenance, media, and research fields. A record can contain the food name, country, coordinates, narrative description, origin food, origin country, connection type, UNESCO status, research links, media URLs, and optional geometry.
tips: Origin fields describe a possible predecessor or source foodway.
Connection Type captures the relationship used by the current data model, such as Trade, Migration, or Colonialism.
Research Links provide the provenance layer for further verification.
Treat historical relationships as claims that should be reviewed against sources, not automatically as proven facts.

title: 7. Timeline & Trade Routes
desc: The Timeline & Trade Routes layer is an AI-assisted historical exploration workspace. It loads foodways_timeline_research.json and presents dated evidence, probable origins, route hypotheses, confidence bands, and a map-based research view.
tips: The year slider filters records using the earliest supported reference available to the research dataset.
Undated records can remain visible through the Show undated option.
Confidence is separated into date, origin, route, and overall dimensions.
Route overlays are explanatory research corridors—not reconstructed historical proof.
Use Refresh Research when a new research JSON has been generated.

title: 8. How to Read Research Evidence
desc: Foodways explicitly distinguishes between curated records and AI-assisted research. Timeline results may include source-backed evidence as well as heuristic hypotheses. The interface labels these distinctions so that users do not confuse exploratory analysis with verified historical reconstruction.
tips: Evidence = a dated or otherwise source-linked claim available in the research payload.
Hypothesis = an AI-assisted interpretation of possible relationships or routes.
Confidence expresses the current strength of the research output, not historical certainty.
Human cross-checking remains the final step before treating a research hypothesis as authoritative.

title: 9. AI Culinary Radar
desc: Foodways can consume the synchronized culinary layer from ai_culinary.json. This research-oriented map surfaces culinary traditions discovered from the broader ICH-Radar workflow and lets Admin users review promising records before saving selected records into the main Supabase inventory.
tips: The layer is designed for discovery and enrichment, not automatic publication.
Use the search box to filter culinary signals by name, country, category, province, or tags.
Open a signal to inspect its description, cultural significance, shared-heritage metadata, and source URLs.
Admin users can use Review & Save to Foodways to curate a record into Supabase.

title: 10. Admin Login & Access
desc: Foodways uses Supabase Auth for account authentication. The current browser flow uses Google OAuth. After sign-in, the application checks the is_foodways_admin database function to determine whether contributor tools should be enabled.
tips: A signed-in user without Admin permission remains a viewer.
Admin status is enforced by the Supabase-backed authorization check.
Do not place private service-role keys in the frontend; the published application uses a public/publishable client key.

title: 11. Creating & Editing Records
desc: Admins can add, edit, and delete Foodways records directly from the application. The editor supports core descriptive fields, origins, geographic coordinates, connection types, media, UNESCO status, research links, and geometry.
tips: New records receive the next Foodways-style identifier when needed.
Editing updates the selected record in the Heritage Foodways Supabase table.
Delete operations require Admin permission and a confirmation step.
Review coordinates and source links carefully before saving.

title: 12. Geographic & Polygon Editing
desc: The Geo Editor allows contributors to define geographic distribution areas and store them as geometry data. This creates a bridge from simple point mapping to richer GIS-compatible heritage documentation.
tips: Use point picking to select latitude/longitude when a precise coordinate is easier to identify on the map.
Polygon geometry is stored in the record and can be included in reporting workflows.
Validate the shape and coordinate order before saving a complex area.

title: 13. Exports & Reporting
desc: Foodways includes several output paths: CSV export for the working dataset, DCMI-oriented metadata export, GeoJSON-compatible spatial output, and PDF profile generation for individual records.
tips: CSV is useful for spreadsheet analysis and archival snapshots.
DCMI output is intended to support digital-library style metadata exchange.
GeoJSON is useful for ArcGIS/QGIS workflows when spatial data is available.
PDF profiles combine narrative information with map snapshots and imagery.

title: 14. Mobile Experience
desc: Devices detected as mobile are redirected to mobile.html. The mobile experience uses a simpler dashboard, bottom navigation, compact search, Leaflet mapping, profile/detail views, and mobile-friendly editing access.
tips: The mobile UI is intentionally less complex than the desktop interface.
Use the bottom navigation to switch between the main mobile views.
Mobile PDF generation is supported for record profiles.
The mobile map and detail panels are designed around touch interaction.

title: 15. Data Architecture
desc: The current application is a static-client architecture backed by Supabase. The browser loads the Heritage Foodways table, applies client-side transformation and rendering, and uses Supabase Auth for session management. Research layers are additionally delivered through versioned JSON files in the repository.
tips: Primary live records: Supabase table Heritage Foodways.
Research cache: foodways_timeline_research.json.
AI culinary layer: ai_culinary.json.
UI guidance: guides.json.
The repository also contains GitHub Actions used for keepalive/research/synchronization workflows.

title: 16. Technology Stack
desc: Foodways deliberately stays close to the browser platform: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, Chart.js, PapaParse, Font Awesome, html2pdf/html2canvas, and Supabase JS. This keeps deployment lightweight and makes the system easy to inspect and extend.
tips: No Node.js build pipeline is required for the main static client.
Maps are rendered with Leaflet.
Charts are rendered with Chart.js.
CSV parsing uses PapaParse.
Authentication and database access use the Supabase JavaScript client.

title: 17. Research Boundaries & Responsible Use
desc: Foodways is both a heritage visualization tool and an exploratory research system. Historical narratives, origins, trade pathways, and AI-discovered signals should be treated according to their evidence status. The app itself warns when research content is heuristic or incomplete.
tips: Do not cite an AI hypothesis as a verified historical fact without human/source review.
Preserve source URLs when curating records.
When publishing research outputs, distinguish evidence, interpretation, and uncertainty.
Use the system as a research accelerator—not as a substitute for specialist historical or heritage scholarship.

title: 18. Troubleshooting
desc: If data fails to load, first check browser connectivity and the Supabase service. If research views are empty, verify that the corresponding JSON file is present and valid. If Admin controls are missing, check the Google sign-in session and the account's Foodways Admin authorization.
tips: A Connection Failed state usually points to a Supabase/network problem.
An empty guide panel usually means guides.json could not be loaded.
Timeline errors can occur when foodways_timeline_research.json is incomplete or unavailable.
AI radar problems can occur if ai_culinary.json is missing or malformed.
After OAuth redirects, reload once if the browser session has not yet propagated.
